I’ll check how `@latest` and `/latest` resolve versions, update the alias behavior, and add a focused regression test. I’m using the repository’s Python style skill.
The SQL registry store returns the first per-stage result for `@latest`, while `/latest` selects the highest numeric version. I’ll make the alias use that same selection rule and cover multiple stages, archived versions, and versions above 9. The existing SQL test fixture runs with workspaces both enabled and disabled.
The regression test reproduced the reported failure: `@latest` returned version 1 when version 2 was in Production. I’ve changed the SQL store to select the highest numeric version and am running the focused checks.
Updated the SQL registry store so `@latest` selects the highest numeric version across all stages, including Archived, matching `/latest`.

Added regression coverage for stage combinations, version 10, case-insensitive aliases, and both workspace modes. Prompt behavior remains unchanged.

Focused tests: **39 passed, 1 skipped**. No dependencies installed or full suite run.

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("alias", ["latest", "LATEST"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "stages",
+    [
+        ["None", "None"],
+        ["None", "Production"],
+        ["Production", "None"],
+        ["Production", "Archived"],
+        ["Archived", "Staging", "Production", "None"],
+        ["None"] * 9 + ["Production"],
+    ],
+)
+def test_get_model_version_by_latest_alias(store, alias, stages):
+    name = "LatestAlias_TestMod"
+    store.create_registered_model(name)
+    for stage in stages:
+        mv = _mv_maker(store, name)
+        store.transition_model_version_stage(name, mv.version, stage, archive_existing_versions=False)
+
+    latest = store.get_model_version_by_alias(name, alias)
+
+    assert int(latest.version) == len(stages)
+    assert latest.current_stage == stages[-1]
+
